faq-a-what-is: BetterBukidnon.org is a free civic website built by volunteers to make public information about the Province of Bukidnon easier to find: provincial offices, officials, hotlines and step-by-step guides. It is part of the BetterGov.ph volunteer ecosystem. It is not an official government website. For official information, visit
faq-q-governor: Who is the Governor of Bukidnon?
faq-a-governor: The Governor is Hon. Rogelio Neil P. Roque, re-elected in May 2025 for the 2025–2028 term. The Vice Governor, who presides over the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (Provincial Board), is Hon. Clive D. Quiño.
faq-q-contact-capitol: How do I contact the Provincial Capitol?
faq-a-contact-capitol: The Provincial Capitol is at the Provincial Capitol Compound, Barangay 9, Malaybalay City, Bukidnon 8700. Offices are open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, except on holidays. The main line is (088) 813-5741.
faq-see-directory: See the phone numbers of provincial offices
faq-q-who-handles: Province, city or municipality: who handles what?
faq-a-who-handles: Bukidnon has two component cities (Malaybalay and Valencia) and 20 municipalities, each with its own city or municipal hall. Civil registration, business permits, barangay clearances, tricycle franchises and public markets are handled by your city or municipal hall, not by the Province. The Provincial Government runs offices such as the Provincial Treasurer, Assessor, Engineer, Health Office and PSWDO.
faq-q-birth-certificate: Where do I get a birth certificate?
faq-a-birth-certificate: Ask the Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO) of the city or municipality where the birth was registered, or get a PSA copy from a PSA outlet or online through PSA Serbilis. Many transactions, such as passport applications, require the PSA copy. Bring a valid government ID. Requirements and fees vary, so confirm with the office.
faq-a-representative-note: Rules on who may request a record differ between the LCRO and PSA. Confirm with the office before you go.
faq-q-business-permit: Where do I get a business permit?
faq-a-business-permit: Business permits (Mayor's permits) are issued by the Business Permits and Licensing Office (BPLO) of the city or municipality where your business is located, not by the Provincial Government. Permits are renewed every year, usually in January. Check the deadline and requirements with your city or municipal hall.
faq-a-business-confirm: Apply at the BPLO of the city or municipality where the business will operate.
faq-a-rpt: It depends on where the property is. For land and buildings in the 20 municipalities, real property tax is a provincial tax: pay it at the treasurer's office of the municipality where the property is located, which collects it for the Province, or ask the Provincial Treasurer's Office. For property in Malaybalay City or Valencia City, pay the city treasurer. Bring your tax declaration or your last official receipt.
faq-a-rpt-discount: Paying for the whole year on or before 31 March may earn a discount where the LGU grants one. Requirements may vary, so confirm with the office.
faq-q-assistance: Where can I ask for financial or medical assistance?
faq-a-assistance: Start with the social welfare office of your city or municipality. The Provincial Social Welfare and Development Office (PSWDO) at the Capitol also handles requests for assistance; call (088) 813-5734 to ask about the requirements.
faq-a-volunteer-2: and tell us how you would like to help: writing, translating into Filipino or Cebuano, checking facts, design or coding. Developers can also contribute on GitHub.
faq-q-languages: What languages is this website available in?
faq-a-languages: English, Filipino and Cebuano (Binisaya). Choose a language with the globe button at the top of each page. Some pages are not fully translated yet; untranslated text appears in English.
